questions.question: Why do indices matter for SQL queries in IRIS?

options.text: They prevent every property from being nullable.
They help IRIS avoid full table scans for common lookups.
They replace all need for query plan analysis.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson explains that without an index, IRIS may need to scan the whole table; with the right index, it can jump directly to matching rows.

questions.question: Which index type is the general-purpose choice for columns that you frequently filter or sort on?
questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson describes the standard index as the default choice for filter and sort access patterns.

questions.question: What is the main additional behavior of a `Unique` index compared with a standard index?

options.text: It stores values only in memory.
It guarantees uniqueness and causes `%Save()` to fail on duplicates.
It is optimized only for aggregate queries.
It can be defined only on numeric properties.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — a unique index both supports lookup and enforces that duplicate values cannot be saved.

questions.question: Which index type is most appropriate for a low-cardinality field such as `Status` or `IsActive`?
questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson explicitly recommends bitmap indices for low-cardinality values like booleans or status fields.

questions.question: Which index type is best suited for aggregate queries such as `AVG(Age)` and range filters on numeric data?
questions.explanation: T1.2 — bitslice indices are presented as the optimized choice for numeric aggregates and range queries.

questions.question: What is the caution given for a key/IDKEY index after data already exists?

options.text: It can only be used on string properties.
It cannot be changed once data already exists.
It is incompatible with SQL queries.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson warns that a key index should be chosen carefully because it cannot be changed after the class already has data.

questions.question: Which index definition is intended for case-insensitive search on `Name`?

options.text: Index NameBitslice On Name [ Type = bitslice ];
Index NameKey On Name [ Type = key ];

questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson uses `%SQLUPPER` in an expression index to support case-insensitive matching.

questions.question: Match each scenario to the most appropriate index strategy. Which choices are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: Email must be unique → Unique index
Frequent filter or sort on Name → Standard index
Status has only a few possible values → Bitmap index
AVG(Age) over a numeric range → Bitslice index
PatientCode should become the object's key → Key/IDKEY index

questions.explanation: T1.2 — these pairings follow the selection table in the lesson: standard for common filter/sort, unique for uniqueness, bitmap for low-cardinality, bitslice for numeric aggregates, and key for a custom primary key.

questions.question: Which operations are described for index maintenance after bulk import or rebuild work? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson lists `%BuildIndices()` for rebuild, targeted rebuild with a list, and `%PurgeIndices()` before rebuilding.

questions.question: When you run `EXPLAIN SELECT ...`, what should you generally hope to see for a well-indexed query?
questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson says to look for an `index scan` instead of a `table scan` in the query plan.
